As per reports, Georgina Rodriguez has adopted the Portuguese legend’s oldest son. Amid all the mess, there are rumors about Cristiano Ronaldo opening up about his oldest son.Has Cristiano Ronaldo reflected on his oldest son’s career and commented on his “laziness”?No, the Portuguese legend Cristiano Ronaldo has not made any such remarks about his oldest son’s career.A fan page on X made a post that read as, “Cristiano Ronaldo was recently quoted saying this about his son: He has no interest in working, yet he still had my card. articles.title: "I remember the pain of losing": Connor McDavid opens up about the brutal pressure he faces as the Edmonton Oilers' captain ahead of the new season
articles.summary: NHL News: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has been with his team for over a decade now as he has remained committed to his role in.
articles.body: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has been with his team for over a decade now as he has remained committed to his role in leading the team. While the Edmonton Oilers have had a brutal run in the last few seasons, Connor McDavid has reflected on the pressure he has had to handle as he witnessed his team losing.Connor McDavid reflects on his responsibilitues in the Edmonton Oilers and the pain of losingIn an essay for The Player’s Tribune, the Edmonton Oilers’ star captain Connor McDavid wrote, “I remember one year, I was like 11 or 12, and we won like 50 games during a season and lost one. On the car ride home, I cried my eyes out to my dad. Looking back, of course, it seems ridiculous now. But I remember the pain of losing, and how at times it felt so much worse than the joy of winning. And if I’m honest, I still struggle with that.”Connor McDavid added, “It’s something I’ve tried to work on a lot these past few seasons. When we lose a game, whether it’s game one of 82 or game 3 of a playoff series, it’s a big deal here. Like I said, I welcome that pressure. But as a player, as a leader, I can’t get too high or too low. And so how do you have fun in an environment like that? I don’t have that answer right now. Sometimes the regular season feels like a grind. I think you’ve seen it in our play this year, in my play.”The popular player continued, “I’m not always proud of that, but I want to be honest here. Because what I can also say is that our room is working really hard. We’re trying to win and have fun and be the team we know we can be. Coach is always telling me to relax, and I don’t always listen to that as much as I should.”Over the last few years, Connor McDavid has led the team with determination and integrity. Though the team’s performance has suffered in the last few years with the Edmonton Oilers’ playoff run ending early when they lost in the first round in the last season, Connor McDavid never gave up on his team.Connor McDavid keeps himself focused on the ice as he stays private with his wife, Lauren KyleAhead of the new season, Connor McDavid has focused on spending time with his wife, Lauren Kyle, as the two prefer to lead private lives.While Lauren Kyle has posted a few updates about their lives on social media, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has completely kept himself out of the spotlight.With the new season beginning in the next few days, all eyes remain on Connor McDavid as he leads the Edmonton Oilers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chasing the Finish Line
articles.summary: CRANE, Texas (KMID/KPEJ) – Crane Native and star athlete Jai Brown has made his name known in the track and field world, dominating the competition. Within t...
articles.body:
CRANE, Texas (KMID/KPEJ) - Crane Native and star athlete Jai Brown has made his name known in the track and field world, dominating the competition. Within the past month Brown has broken three state records while competting at this year Texas Amateur Athletic Federation meet in the 100M, 200M, and Long Jump.

"When he gets into the mode, he goes very quiet, very silent," Mother Rausalyn Brown said. "You can't get no conversation out of him."

It's that focus and killer instinct that has got Brown to where he is today. As for his mother Rausalyn, she was a star athlete herself being a two-time state champion during her time at Crane High School. Father Khaled Brown was an athlete himself, playing college footbal at Waylan Baptist University.

Sticking with the athletic gene within the family, Brown's Great Grandmother Daisy Jeffery was a member of the early 1970s Sul Ross Volleyball national championship team. Jeffery was named to the universities sports hall of fame a few years ago. In addition Jai's uncle, aunts, and grandfather have all competed at the junior olympics.

After blazing through each event, Brown went on to nationals in Iowa, where he would experience a challenge. Although Brown has blown away his oppenents on the track, it was a close call in the 200M race that nearly gave him his first loss.

"I felt nervous because I thought I lost," Brown said.

However just as any champion does, Brown pushed his way through diving for the finish line. As Brown headed to the medical tent to clean up a wound he suffered from the dive, it was there he found out he had won. In addition to winning the 200m, Brown also competed and won in the 100M and Long Jump.

With both the athletic gift and competitive mindset, it is the support that Jai recieves that really motivates him.

"The support is very great," Brown said. "I love that I'm being loved by everyone, even my coach, even my family. I just love that everybody's supporting me."

When it all comes down to how far Brown wants to go with the first, the goal is straight and simple, the olympics.

articles.title: UNC continues investigation into football program allegations
articles.summary: The circus rolls on despite any positive vibes from last week’s win.
articles.body:
With the news earlier this evening that Michael Lombardi has resigned as General Manager, WRAL has reported that UNC is still looking into a number of allegations surrounding the football program. The allegations are quite serious, and would almost certainly be enough for several more people to lose their jobs.

According to WRAL, lawyers are investigating whether defensive coordinator Steve Belichick used drugs while on the job or provided drugs to a player on the team. The younger Belichick has been on leave since over the summer for undisclosed reasons.

There is also an investigation into the existence of inappropriate relationships between recruiting staff and a player as well as assistant coaches and recruiting staff. WRAL notes that those questioned in the matter were asked whether or not they'd reported any issues to Bill Belichick.

If there is indeed validity to these claims, particularly if it is confirmed that Bill Belichick was made aware of what was going on within his program, it seems likely that the entire house of cards may fall. While it's clear that Lombardi was a real problem, the school is concerned enough that he was not the root of the entire problem to keep digging into what was going on in the Kenan Football Center.

Some of the allegations simply feel too big to recover from if they are proven to be true. It's a significant black eye on the program and the university that there is enough smoke to even reach this point. Almost the entire Bill Belichick Experience has been a punchline in the college football world, and all of the detractors were just given a boatload more fuel for the fire.

articles.title: What is De'Zhaun Stribling's role as 'big part' of 49ers offense?
articles.summary: The hype around San Francisco 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling continues to rise as the 2026 NFL season draws nearer.
articles.body:
As the season draws nearer, De'Zhaun Stribling's role in the San Francisco 49ers offense is beginning to look clearer.

Speaking on the "49ers Talk" podcast with NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy singled out the rookie's habits early in camp and noted that he'll play a big part in the team's offense in 2026.

"He's done an amazing job with coming in and, um, obviously learning the playbook and just keeping his head down and working," Purdy said. "... he's going to be a big part of our offense this year, so I'm excited to see him play."

As for how he fits into the offense, The Athletic 's Matt Barrows believes Stribling is primed to be the primary slot receiver and "Mike Evans' understudy at X," while Deebo Samuel will play the Z receiver role on the strong side of the formation.

Barrows noted that all of San Francisco's receivers are expected to be cross-trained across the three spots, but that Stribling's clearest early path to snaps runs through the slot, with added reps as Evans' backup on the outside.

The 49ers used the No. 33 overall pick on Stribling in this year's draft, the first selection of the second round, after he closed out his college career at Ole Miss with 261 receptions, 2,964 yards and 23 touchdowns across stints at Washington State, Oklahoma State and Ole Miss. His 4.36-second 40-yard dash at the combine reinforced the vertical speed teams covet, even if his projected role leans more toward the slot to start.

Stribling finished the preseason with 11 catches on 13 targets for 109 yards in the two games he played. He sat out the final preseason game while recovering from a minute shoulder injury.

Between Purdy's public endorsement of his work ethic and Barrows' outline of a multi-spot role, Stribling looks like he's carving out real involvement in the offense early in his rookie season — even if the bulk of his snaps come from the slot rather than as an outside X or Z option.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's record-breaking August sets the stage for her FIBA Women's World Cup debut
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark set multiple WNBA records in August, scoring or assisting on 44.7 points per game and more before her FIBA Women's World Cup debut.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark is gearing up for her first appearance in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup on Friday, and if she plays like she did for the Indiana Fever this past month, Team USA may be impossible to take down. Clark’s August in the WNBA was a spectacle to behold, as she once again made league history with her phenomenal play. For starters, Clark scored or assisted on 44.7 points per game, a WNBA record for a single month. The stellar point guard has always had a knack for either finding the bottom of the net or dishing assists to her teammates to get the job done. CAITLIN CLARK, INDIANA FEVER GO INTO FIBA WORLD CUP BREAK WITH BIG WIN OVER CONNECTICUT Either way, those numbers were racked up throughout the month of August, and more history followed. Clark became the first player in WNBA history with back-to-back 30-plus-point and 10-plus-assist games. They both came in the final two games for the Fever before this international break, scoring 34 points with 12 assists in a 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun. Then, Clark poured in 37 points, including eight of 12 three-pointers made, with 10 assists in the Aug. 23 win over the Chicago Sky, 113-90. That game against the Sky was also significant, as Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from the Wintrust Arena in Chicago after an altercation involving Sky guard Natasha Cloud. The third-quarter incident, though, never rattled Clark and the Fever, and they got the job done before heading back home. USA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL ROSTER REVEAL FOR FIBA WORLD CUP FEATURES AWKWARD CAITLIN CLARK, ANGEL REESE PAIRING It's also worth mentioning the off-the-court situation that made national headlines involving Freedom considering the Fever's caption called Clark's performance "HERstoric." Kanter, fellow Fever star Sophie Cunningham, and many others have spoken out about their belief that biological men should be out of women's sports. Meanwhile, a WNBA task force of team presidents and general managers met last month to discuss a wide range of topics, one of which being transgender athletes. However, they did not arrive at any eligibility rules, which basically means the league can't define what a woman is. "Today's meeting covered a wide range of topics, including ongoing discussions on transgender athletes and the continued hate and vitriol directed at players online," the WNBA’s statement read. "We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months. We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others." WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS So, while play on words does make sense here with "HERstoric," it falls a bit flat considering what's been happening off the court with the WNBA. But there's no doubting the history that Clark continues to make. Clark put together five games in August where she had at least 20 points and 10 assists. To put that into perspective, no other player had five such games in the last five seasons combined. Finally, Clark averaged 24.4 points per game, which was the highest-scoring month by a point guard in WNBA history. The Fever went 7-4 in their August stretch, bringing them to 26-14 on the season thus far. That record is good for fifth in the WNBA standings, though it is quite tight between those in front, and behind, Indiana. Clark and the rest of her teammates will be sure to hit the ground running and try to get hot heading into the playoffs.

articles.title: ‘AAF risk’: Herbal supplements put India’s Asian Games athletes under scanner
articles.summary: More sports News: Bengaluru: With Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) officials conducting random checks on India’s elite athletes preparing for the Asian Games, experts are.
articles.body: Bengaluru: With Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) officials conducting random checks on India’s elite athletes preparing for the Asian Games, experts are concerned that the use of herbal supplements by top athletes could result in Adverse Analytical Findings (AAF) when samples are tested for performance-enhancing substances at WADA-accredited laboratories abroad.According to experts, the use of herbal supplements is quite common among athletes training in national camps.“Among the supplements commonly used by our athletes are kida jadi buti, bhasmas, ashwagandha and shilajit. Kida jadi (Cordyceps sinensis) is the most expensive of the lot, retailing at Rs 16-20 lakh per kilogram. It is consumed after being mixed with honey,” they told TOI.In India, kida jadi is listed on e-commerce platforms at around Rs 1.66 lakh for 100g.“There are many athletes who use their savings to buy kida jadi and consume it regularly. There is a risk of an AAF for athletes using herbal supplements, as many of these products are not tested for their ingredients. For a month’s course, they may have to shell out around Rs 1 lakh.“A lot of our sprinters, throwers and middle-distance runners are taking these supplements,” they said, adding that most athletes do not disclose their use of herbal supplements when declaring the list of supplements they consume.Kida jadi is a type of fungus sourced from the Himalayas. Indian athletes have been using it for many years and none have returned a positive result so far. However, there have recently been concerns that some products may contain substances on WADA’s banned list, though nothing has been confirmed yet.“These metabolites may not have triggered a positive result in NADA tests, but in advanced tests conducted by the AIU, the outcome could be different, putting our athletes at risk of an AAF,” experts said.Asked about the use of locally sourced herbal supplements, Mihira Khopkar, who served as the Indian contingent’s nutritionist at the Paris Olympics, confirmed the risks involved.“In elite sport, it is almost non-negotiable that high-performing athletes choose supplements that are not only evidence-based but also third-party tested,” she told TOI.Unprecedented scrutinyAthletics coaches, both former and current, who have followed India’s progress over the past few decades, recalled that Indian athletes have never undergone such intense testing before a major Games.“What the AIU has done on behalf of WADA is targeted testing of India’s top athletes who will be competing at the Asian Games. Across Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar and Patiala, officials have tested most athletes in the squad. This is the first time they have conducted such large-scale random testing of Indian athletes ahead of a major meet,” sources told TOI.“A few years ago, WADA attempted to test Indian athletes training in Potchefstroom, South Africa, but achieved limited success as many were unavailable. Athletes cannot be penalised for missing random tests, unlike those in the Registered Testing Pool (RTP), who are bound by the whereabouts clause,” they added.After testing athletes residing at the Kalinga Stadium complex in Bhubaneswar, officials also conducted checks on those training in Bengaluru at the Anju Bobby Sports Foundation and the SAI South Centre.India topped the AIU’s list of doping offenders in July this year with 162 names, ahead of Kenya (148) and Russia (60). The AIU also reclassified the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) from Category B to Category A.“Unfortunately, the quality of the domestic anti-doping programme is simply not proportionate to the doping risk,” AIU Chair David Howman had said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Treesa-Gayatri’s coach missing from list, WFI finally clears foreign coaches
articles.summary: Badminton News: New Delhi: India’s latest women’s doubles hope, BWF World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, will head to the Asian G.
articles.body: New Delhi: India’s latest women’s doubles hope, BWF World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, will head to the Asian Games without their dedicated coach B Sumeeth Reddy, whose name does not figure in the official coaching and support staff list for badminton, while the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) has finally agreed to send all three foreign coaches despite its initial reluctance, following a Sports Authority of India (SAI) rebuke.Reddy, a former Olympian who retired in March 2025, has specifically worked with Treesa and Gayatri since then, while also overseeing other women’s doubles players at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad. He was a constant presence in their coaching corner at international events and during the recent Worlds in New Delhi, sitting alongside Gopichand and guiding the pair through their matches.Treesa and Gayatri ended India’s 15-year wait for a women’s doubles medal at the Worlds since 2011, producing a string of impressive performances to claim bronze.Their Asian Games place had earlier come under scrutiny after sports authorities questioned their selection against the prescribed criteria, with Priya Konjengbam and Shruti Mishra emerging as alternatives. Badminton Association of India (BAI) defended the selection on rankings and recent performances.TOI contacted a senior federation official to ascertain whether Reddy’s name had originally been forwarded to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) as an official women’s doubles coach. A call to a BAI official did not elicit a response.It has been learnt that Gopichand will carry the primary responsibility of guiding Treesa and Gayatri in Reddy’s absence. Tan Kim Her, who specifically works with Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, could assist the women’s pair if schedules do not clash. South Korean Yong Sung Yoo, Lakshya Sen’s personal coach has received clearance. Twelve coaching and support personnel have been named for the 20-member badminton team.WFI finally relents on foreign coachesFor wrestling’s 16-member squad, 14 coaching and support personnel have been listed, with all three foreign coaches now set to travel: Georgia’s Emzarios Bentinidis (men’s freestyle), Russia’s Gogi Koguashvili (greco-roman) and Japan’s Kosei Akaishi (women’s team). WFI had initially resisted sending them, preferring Indian coaches over them, but agreed after SAI questioned their omission.Only seven grooms in equestrianAccording to sources, the Equestrian Federation of India’s (EFI) ad-hoc committee had proposed 20 grooms for the eight-member equestrian team, but only seven have received clearance. articles.summary: LSU at Center of College Football’s Latest Eligibility Battle The LSU Tigers have found themselves at the center of one of the biggest controversies in colle...
articles.body:
LSU at Center of College Football's Latest Eligibility Battle

The LSU Tigers have found themselves at the center of one of the biggest controversies in college football just days before their highly anticipated season opener against Clemson.

The dispute involves LSU head coach Lane Kiffin and the school's decision to pursue former NFL players who are attempting to return to college football. Former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris are among the players hoping to join the Tigers after spending time in the NFL.

The SEC has strongly opposed LSU's plans. On Thursday, the conference filed a federal lawsuit against LSU, its administration and Kiffin, arguing that the Tigers are violating conference rules that prohibit athletes who have signed professional contracts from returning to college competition. The SEC is seeking an injunction to prevent LSU from moving forward with the former professionals.

LSU, however, received a major boost in court Thursday night. East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, clearing the way for former NFL players to be included on LSU's roster while the larger eligibility dispute continues through the courts.

The ruling could have major implications beyond Baton Rouge. More than 40 athletes across college sports are involved in the broader eligibility dispute, making the case an important test of how far athletes can go between college and professional sports under the NCAA's evolving rules.

The SEC has argued that allowing former professionals to return would undermine the distinction between college and professional athletics. Conference commissioner Greg Sankey has defended the league's position, while LSU and the athletes involved have argued that players should not be punished by eligibility rules that have changed while they were pursuing professional opportunities.

For Kiffin, the controversy comes at an especially important time. LSU enters the 2026 season ranked No. 11 nationally and is preparing to host Clemson in one of the weekend's biggest games.

What began as an attempt to add experienced players to LSU's roster has now become a major legal battle involving LSU, the SEC and the NCAA. With the Tigers' season opener approaching, the outcome could affect not only Kiffin's roster but the future of college football eligibility itself.

For LSU, the message is clear: the fight is no longer just about two players — it could help determine where the line between college and professional football is drawn.

articles.title: Ryan Coleman-Williams Could Be Poised for His Best Season Yet at Alabama
articles.summary: The Crimson Tide’s electric playmaker is trading highlight-reel flashes for disciplined consistency, aiming to transform his undeniable raw speed into a domi...
articles.body:
Ryan Coleman-Williams does not need to remind anyone how talented he is.

We saw it when he arrived at Alabama as a teenager and almost immediately became one of the most electric players in college football. We have seen the speed, the body control, the ability to turn an ordinary play into a touchdown and the kind of natural talent that simply cannot be coached.

But heading into his junior season at Alabama, Coleman-Williams appears to be chasing something different: consistency.

And if he finds it, 2026 might not simply be a bounce-back season. It could be the best season of his Alabama career.

"My main focus is trying to be a consistent guy day in and day out," Coleman-Williams said at SEC Media Days this summer. "With the work that I put in, the results will show for themselves."

That statement probably tells us more about where Coleman-Williams is entering Year 3 than any preseason ranking or highlight reel ever could. Because talent has never been the question. The question now is whether Coleman-Williams can become the complete, dependable, dominant receiver Alabama knows he can be.

And there is plenty of reason to believe he is ready to do exactly that.

Coleman-Williams' freshman season was one of the most exciting introductions Alabama fans have seen from a wide receiver in years. He finished the 2024 season with 48 receptions for 865 yards and eight receiving touchdowns while averaging an incredible 18 yards per reception. He also added 48 rushing yards and two more touchdowns on the ground.

He was explosive. He was fearless. And perhaps most impressively, he was doing all of it while being one of the youngest players in college football.

There were moments during that season when it seemed almost impossible to believe how young he was. Coleman-Williams could line up across from some of the best defensive backs in America and look completely comfortable. He could beat defenders vertically, make difficult catches in traffic and create explosive plays after the catch.

That freshman season created enormous expectations. Maybe unfair expectations.

By the time his sophomore season arrived, Coleman-Williams wasn't simply viewed as another talented Alabama receiver anymore. He was expected to be one of the best players in college football. He entered 2025 with preseason All-American recognition from several major outlets and landed on watch lists for the Maxwell, Walter Camp, Biletnikoff and Hornung Awards.

Everyone expected another massive season.

Instead, it became a year filled with flashes of greatness mixed with frustrating inconsistency. Coleman-Williams still finished the season with 49 receptions for 689 yards and four touchdowns. Those are certainly not bad numbers. But compared to what he accomplished as a freshman, and compared to the expectations placed on him entering the year, it felt like a step backward. His receiving yardage dropped by nearly 200 yards, his touchdown total was cut in half and the explosive plays did not come quite as consistently.

Drops also became part of the conversation.

Coleman-Williams had 13 drops in 2025 after only four during his freshman season. There were still reminders of exactly how dangerous he could be. Look at what happened against Wisconsin. Coleman-Williams caught five passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns, including scoring receptions of 75 and 41 yards. He accumulated 109 yards after the catch in that game alone.

That was Ryan Coleman-Williams at his best.

Explosive. Dynamic. Almost impossible to contain once he gets into space.

The challenge is bringing that version of himself every Saturday. And that appears to be exactly what he has spent the offseason working toward.

Kalen DeBoer has repeatedly mentioned the progress Coleman-Williams has made.

After Alabama's A-Day scrimmage, DeBoer specifically pointed to consistency as one of the biggest improvements he had seen.

"Ryan's consistency was something all spring long that I know he should be feeling good about," DeBoer said. "Ryan's expectations are just like all of ours, that we expect elite performance."

DeBoer went even further, calling Coleman-Williams a leader and saying he "works as hard as anyone that's out there."

That matters. Because Coleman-Williams is not the young freshman phenom anymore. He is now one of the veterans.

Alabama's official roster lists him as a 6-foot, 184-pound junior entering his third season in Tuscaloosa. He has played in 27 games over his first two seasons and already owns 97 career receptions for 1,554 yards and 12 receiving touchdowns.

We talk about Coleman-Williams as though there is still so much left for him to accomplish, and there is, but he has already produced more than 1,500 receiving yards before beginning his junior season.

Now imagine what happens if everything starts coming together.

Imagine the freshman-year explosiveness combined with junior-year maturity. Imagine the speed and athleticism combined with more dependable hands. Imagine the spectacular catches combined with consistent execution on the routine ones. That is the player Alabama could have in 2026.

And that player would be one of the best receivers in America.

There are signs throughout the offseason suggesting that Coleman-Williams understands exactly what is at stake. DeBoer has said he has been "as locked in as you could ever imagine" and praised his ability to focus on the areas he can control.

Coleman-Williams even chose to stay in Tuscaloosa during a May window when players had an opportunity to return home, continuing his work in preparation for what could be a defining season.

Those things matter to me. Everyone sees what happens inside Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturdays. We don't always see the months of work before those Saturdays arrive.

The extra reps. The film study. The conditioning. The routes run when nobody is watching. The work on catching mechanics. The decision to stay around Tuscaloosa when you could easily go home. Those are the things that can take a naturally gifted football player and turn him into a truly great one.

Coleman-Williams also appears physically more prepared than he was a season ago.

DeBoer has noted that he has been healthier during the offseason, understands his body better and has added weight, something the Alabama coach believes should help him in multiple areas. Then there is what has been happening during fall camp.

Offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb offered one of the more eye-opening comments of the preseason after Coleman-Williams made a huge play during practice.

"He caught (an) 80-yard drive in practice, touchdown to finish. Unbelievable catch. Enough said," Grubb said. Sometimes it really is that simple. We already know Coleman-Williams can make those plays. The question has always been whether Alabama can get those plays consistently.

If the answer in 2026 is yes, look out. The opportunity will certainly be there.

Alabama enters the season with Coleman-Williams and Lotzeir Brooks established as the top two options in the wide receiver room. Brooks caught 32 passes for 441 yards as a freshman and emerged as another legitimate weapon for the Crimson Tide.

That could actually help Coleman-Williams. Defenses cannot simply dedicate every resource to stopping No. 1 if Brooks and the rest of Alabama's receiving corps continue developing. And with Keelon Russell taking over at quarterback, having a veteran receiver like Coleman-Williams could be invaluable.

Young quarterbacks need players they can trust. They need someone who can win one-on-one matchups. Someone who can turn a short completion into an explosive gain. Someone they can throw to on third down when everybody in the stadium knows where the football might be going.

Coleman-Williams has the ability to become that guy. Not merely Alabama's most talented receiver.

That distinction is important. Talent gets attention. Dependability wins football games.

If Alabama needs six yards on third-and-five, can Coleman-Williams make the catch? If the Crimson Tide is trailing late on the road in the SEC, can Russell trust him to win his matchup? If Alabama gets a one-on-one opportunity downfield, can Coleman-Williams turn it into six points?

Those moments will ultimately determine how his junior season is remembered. And I believe he is better prepared for those moments than he has ever been.

There is another part of Coleman-Williams' story heading into 2026 that feels significant.

He is now wearing No. 1 and has added Coleman, his mother's last name, to his name. He explained this spring that he wants to write his own legacy and that his mother is an important part of that legacy. In a strange way, that feels appropriate for where he is in his career.

Ryan Coleman-Williams isn't the 17-year-old sensation anymore.

He isn't simply the young kid everyone is amazed by.

He has experienced success. He has experienced criticism. He has experienced expectations. He has experienced adversity. And now he gets to show everyone what he learned from all of it.

That might ultimately be what makes 2026 special.

Sometimes a player's best season does not happen when everything is easy. Sometimes it happens after being humbled a little.

After experiencing frustration. After hearing the criticism. After realizing talent alone isn't enough. Coleman-Williams' sophomore season was not a failure. Far from it.

Most receivers in college football would gladly take 49 catches for 689 yards. But Coleman-Williams isn't most receivers.

We have seen his ceiling. We know what he can become. And more importantly, he knows it too.

That is why the word "consistency" matters so much. Coleman-Williams doesn't need another viral highlight to prove he is talented.

He doesn't need another spectacular catch to convince NFL scouts that he possesses rare ability.

What he needs now is week-after-week production.

Five catches here. Seven catches there. A touchdown when Alabama needs one. A third-down conversion. A contested catch.

Blocking hard when the football isn't coming his way. Doing the little things over and over and over again. That is how good players become great players. And that is why I believe Ryan Coleman-Williams could be headed toward his best season yet.

The talent is still there. The explosiveness is still there. The experience is now there. But perhaps most importantly, the maturity appears to be there too.

Alabama doesn't need Coleman-Williams to become somebody different in 2026. It needs him to become the most consistent version of the player we already know he can be.

If he does that, 865 receiving yards might no longer be his career high. Eight touchdowns might not be either. And by the time this season is over, we may look back at Coleman-Williams' sophomore struggles as exactly what helped prepare him for what came next.

Ryan Coleman-Williams has already shown college football how special he can be. Now comes the opportunity to show it every single week.

And if this offseason is any indication, Year 3 might just be the year everything comes together.

articles.title: 3 takeaways as Wisconsin volleyball defeats Auburn without Grace Egan
articles.summary: Halle Thompson's 11 kills and Eva Travis' 10 kills led Wisconsin volleyball to a three-set win over Auburn while missing a few other key players.
articles.body:
MADISON – Wisconsin volleyball did not always make it look easy, but the Badgers went 2-0 in the Big Ten/SEC Challenge.

Fewer than 24 hours after the five-set thriller against No. 17 Florida , the fifth-ranked Badgers defeated unranked Auburn , 25-23, 25-17, 25-20, on Sept. 3 at the UW Field House. The match had 17 ties and eight lead changes before UW prevailed in each set to improve its 2026 record to 3-3.

"We're playing a lot of really, really close sets, and things happen," Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said after the match. "There's a back-and-forth element to it, and we're growing. … I like where we're at. I like how we're learning."

Here are three takeaways from UW's latest win:

Wisconsin women's volleyball vs. Florida at the UW Field House

Audrey Flanagan, Eva Travis, Grace Lopez and Lynney Tarnow have all either led or shared the lead for kills in a match so far this season for the Badgers.

It was Halle Thompson's turn against Auburn.

The freshman outside hitter earned a spot in the starting lineup and led the Badgers with 11 kills. The last of those kills secured the third set. (It was easily a career-high for the freshman, whose previous career-high was four kills against then-No. 4 Pittsburgh.)

While Sheffield saw Thompson's trademark aggressiveness – "there's no set that she doesn't think she can get a kill on" – she also was "smart" in her attacking.

"Halle's like a double shot of espresso," Sheffield said. "I wanted to make sure that we weren't sleepy out there and the building wasn't sleepy. … The kid was pretty hyped, and that worked well attacking wise."

While her .200 hitting percentage will not necessarily jump off the page, her 30 total attacks were valuable in the latter part of the Badgers' back-to-back matches in the Big Ten/SEC Challenge.

"We needed her," Sheffield said. "We needed those swings. We needed her 30 swings. … The first two sets, she really set the tone with the areas of the court that she was attacking."

She was not the only outside hitter to stand out against Auburn, though. Travis had 10 kills while hitting .286 and earning praise from Sheffield afterward for her maturity and confidence after past attack errors. It was the UC-Santa Barbara transfer's third match with 10-plus kills so far in 2026.

The Badgers hit .305 as a whole, compared to Auburn's .196.

Why Wisconsin's blocking was better than stats might suggest

Auburn finished the match with a 5-4 advantage in total blocks, but Wisconsin left the UW Field House with a reason to be optimistic about its blocking. It goes back to one of the common threads Sheffield sees among good teams.

But Sheffield believes that "every really good team does something to stress out people." In Auburn's case, it was how quickly they set its left pin.

"It forces you to make choices defensively," Sheffield said. "So it kind of gets you out of your base defensive position, especially your block."

Wisconsin's blockers, Sheffield believes, "did a really good job" against the Tigers when considering the circumstances.

"I thought we set up in really good positions," Sheffield said. "We didn't get tooled. We didn't get used very much. … We were really disciplined with our hands."

The Badgers' success came with Natalie Wardlow and Lynney Tarnow starting at the middle blocker positions. Wardlow had eight kills, and Tarnow had seven kills. Wardlow had a much more involved role in the Auburn win than she did on Sept. 2 against Florida.

"My mindset is always like, 'How can I be good for the team and not getting so internal into myself,'" Wardlow said.

Wisconsin misses Jaela Auguste, Grace Egan in win over Auburn

Wisconsin's three-set sweep was despite the absences of two key players.

Jaela Auguste missed her fourth consecutive match with an injury. When asked earlier in the week whether it was a continuation of the abdominal strain that kept her out of the exhibition, Sheffield said "possibly" with a wink.

Grace Egan, meanwhile, did not play for the second time in a three-match stretch. Unlike her absence against then-No. 4 Pittsburgh – one that Sheffield later said was a "coach's decision" – Egan was not on the sidelines.

"She wasn't there," Sheffield said after the Auburn match. "Undisclosed injury, and we'll keep it at that."

Right-side hitter Grace Lopez, who missed all of last season with a knee injury, also did not play against the Tigers. She did appear in two sets against Florida as a serving specialist, subbing in for libero Anna Bardaro.

"It's not fun missing some people," Sheffield said. "You like to be at full strength, but that just doesn't happen. I don't know how football coaches do it. Every time that you go out and take the field, it's like the Revolutionary War or something like that. … We've had a few, and we've had to deal with it. But on the other side of that is opportunity."

articles.title: Ajit Agarkar absent from key BCCI review meeting: Why did the chief selector miss it?
articles.summary: The absence of Ajit Agarkar from the BCCI review meeting has raised questions about why the chief selector wasn't present.
articles.body:
Ajit Agarkar missed a BCCI review meeting in Mumbai, sparking rumors about his future as chief selector.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia claimed the former Indian pacer was overseas with a poor phone signal, denying any rift.

Agarkar remains contracted until July 2027 and is expected to attend the Duleep Trophy final in Chennai on September 6.

Ajit Agarkar's absence at the Mumbai review meeting was enough to spark rumors

BCCI chief selector Ajit Agarkar's missing a high-level board meeting in his hometown of Mumbai was always going to set off alarms, no matter how hard the officials tried to play it down. When the chief selector vanishes from an executive review, speculations are bound to take off immediately.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia was quick to start the damage control. He insisted that Agarkar was simply stuck overseas with terrible cell service. He also pointed out that the meeting was called on short notice, with no selection business on the table.

But the timing couldn't be worse, coming right after reports that top board officials had stepped in when Agarkar's panel suggested Rohit Sharma step down from red-ball cricket.

Why did Agarkar miss the BCCI review meeting?

Whether Agarkar was genuinely off the grid or just caught in an administrative scheduling mess, the incident highlights how fragile his position looks from the outside. For now, the board insists his contract through July 2027 is safe, but he will be watched closely when he surfaces for the Duleep Trophy final in Chennai on September 6.

Devajit Saikia was quick to offer a defensive explanation for why Agarkar couldn't even log on to a video call, framing the absence as a simple matter of poor logistics.

"Today, he was out of station, so he could not be a part of the meeting," Saikia said . "The meeting was called at very short notice, and our chairman of the selection committee, Ajit, was not in town. So he could not join the meeting, and he was in an area where he could not join online either, despite our best efforts."

Saikia also tried to shut down talk that Agarkar's job was on the line. "Today, we did not have any selection meeting. There was no such discussion in today's meeting," Saikia added. "I do not want to give any fodder to the speculators."

The Cricket News Opinion: Agarkar has been sidelined by the board, and everyone knows it

The moment the BCCI overrode Agarkar and his selection panel over Rohit Sharma's retirement, they effectively clipped his wings. Once a chief selector is publicly seen as someone who can be overruled by board executives on major calls, his authority is shot.

Asking people to believe that the most powerful selector in Indian cricket couldn't find a phone signal to join a crucial meeting in 2026 sounds like a bad excuse. It makes Agarkar look isolated, whether he actually was or not.

If the BCCI wants Agarkar to run Indian selection through the 2027 World Cup, they need to let him actually select. A chief selector who gets blocked when trying to transition senior players out is just a figurehead, and until Agarkar gets the backing to make the hard calls, every meeting he misses will be read as a sign that the board is pulling the strings without him.

articles.title: Bloomington South volleyball stays perfect with sweep of North
articles.summary: Middle Quinn Reynolds hard to stop as Panthers open season 12-0 with tough win over Cougars.
articles.body:
Which means the Panthers' opponents do, too, when it comes to aligning their defense.

On Thursday, Sept. 3, South's best choice was to set senior middle Quinn Reynolds , who had 16 kills, everything from dunks and tips high above the crowd at the net to lasers from the back row, as the undefeated Panthers swept rival North, 25-19, 25-21, 25-19 at the Cougar Den.

Bloomington North volleyball welcomes South | Our best photos

"Our team, you can put the ball anywhere on the floor and trust that it's being taken care of," South coach Emma Abplanalp said. "She's a great leader on this team, they're all so supportive. They all want to win. They all want to be the best.

"So I think that really helps them feel confident in each other so they're able to play loose and play free and know that we're in this together."

Every Clark, Lily Reinhart and Ella Alley kept the block busy when Reynolds' number wasn't called. Junior Ola Parker, the new setter with returning starter Harper Rahn, is also settling in, making thing smoother.

"It helps to have a team that has multiple weapons," North coach Sami Ferachi said. "You've just got to learn how to defend it. At the end of the day, everyone is just a high school girl. Everyone's got their weaknesses.

"No one's playing in college right now. Everyone has room to grow, so you just have to find what those weaknesses are an expose them. And the quicker you find them the quicker you can win games. They had the upper hand tonight."

And South thinks it still has more in the tank if there's a sectional rematch.

"We definitely didn't play our game as much as we normally do," Abplanalp said. "This game, so much hype around it. I try to treat it as normal a game as possible, but you can't help it. The crowd is full. It's loud in here.

"I think (North) definitely had some competitive edges to them, but I don't think we played to our full potential as well."

That's something that will get tested more and more as the win streak continues for the 12-0 Panthers.

"I feel like we're showing everyone the hard work that we're putting in in the gym," Reynolds said. "The way we're able to take what we built on last year and continue to grow and be really successful this season."

The record is still perfect, but there are still flaws to work on.

South's had some big wins during its run, including a five-setter (with a reverse sweep) at 3A power Northview and overpowered Brownstown Central 25-18, 25-16, 25-12, their first win over the Braves since 2022.

Each win just makes the target on their backs bigger. South is 40-7 since the beginning of the 2025 season.

"I feel like definitely after we beat Brownstown, it was a big confidence boost to us," Reynolds said. "That was exciting for us, and I feel like we're just going to keep growing the streak. But we also need to remember the streak doesn't really matter; we just want to make sure we're really strong for sectionals."

Adding to the excitement level, there seemed to be a game within a game all night as Reynolds and North junior outside Olivia Bargen (13 kills) took turns seeing who could hit the hardest screamer.

"I'm glad we got to see a big swing tonight," Abplanalp said. "That's the first game we've seen someone really put the ball away. But I'm really proud of our defense. Even if it wasn't a perfect up-ball, that we were scrapping and played well."

Bargen is leading the Cougars in kills this year and showed why.

"She was determined to come in this year and be an all-around outside," Ferachi said. "She's put in the extra reps, the extra work. She's got the headspace for it. She wants to be a leader for our team. So that's 90% of the battle right there to be the outside that she is.

"The other 10% is what she physically capable of. We love her."

The Cougars were game all night, but South, after getting past some first-set jitters/communication issues, never let North gain much traction. North would fight and hang around, coming from down 17-10 to 22-19 in Set 1, down 20-15 to 22-21 in Set 2 and down 20-13 to 21-17 in Set 3.

"We want scrappy play but calm, scrappy play," Abplanalp said. "And tonight, our emotions got the best of is a little bit, a little more chaotic. But as the sets went on, we got better at controlling that."

All three times, South polished off the sets, showing it has a killer instinct. Three kills in a row by Reynolds finished Set 1, kills by Clark, Reynolds and an ace by Neely Warner ended Set 2 and a block and three kills, the last by Reynolds, ended the night.

"We tried to stay really calm through this," Reynolds said. "We knew coming in we had to stay calm and play our game. The energy in the gym was loud, but it was fun to feed off it."

North is not focused on its 3-5 record as much as its growth over the first eight matches, which has included tough losses to Floyd Central, Brownstown, Columbus North and now South.

"You can't make your identity about your record," Ferachi said. "It's really fun to say that you're 12-0, but at the end of the day, you have to have the confidence in your team and the work that you're putting in and that's where we're at. Record has a story, but we know what our story is."

Bargen was a presence offensively all night, but it took some time to get others involved as consistently. North opened things up for Emma Rice, who responded well off the right side, while Aubrey Grupenhoff, Hollie Northcutt, Rayne Nelson and Ashley Stegmoller got some licks in as well.

"Emma asked for some feedback for what shots were open, what could she do to score for us," Ferachi said. "She made adjustments and it happened. We've got very coachable people on our team."

It just wasn't enough but North plans to change that by late October.

"None of us were dissatisfied with how hard we fought," Ferachi said. "Our response to being pushed, we were proud of how we kept going, kept attacking.

"This is the eighth game of our season, but we're thinking of the long game. So we're going to take what areas they exposed in our play and we're going to get better at it."

articles.title: Misha Donskov Reveals How Mike Babcock Recruited Him To Oilers
articles.summary: The Edmonton Oilers made several new hires during the offseason, which include head coach Mike Babcock and DJ Smith to replace the terminated Kris Knoblauch...
articles.body:
The Edmonton Oilers made several new hires during the offseason, which include head coach Mike Babcock and DJ Smith to replace the terminated Kris Knoblauch and Mark Stuart.

Another hiring that the Oilers made was bringing aboard Hockey Canada's Misha Donskov as a coaching consultant in late August.

Having previously worked with Babcock before on the international stage, Donskov revealed it was Babcock who reached out to him to join the Oilers.

"It is a unique opportunity. I've know Mike (Babcock) for over 10 years. I was fortunate to be on his staff at the 2016 World Cup of Hockey," he said via Jason Gregor on X. "Babs reached out to me in the summer and laid out this opportunity. We went back and forth and then I met Stan Bowman in Edmonton when I was in town for the Hlinka/Gretzky tournament. My role is about sharing my ideas and information from my experience Internationally and in the NHL. I will be in Edmonton roughly six days a month and then the rest of the month I will be supporting the staff remotely. I've also coached with DJ (Smith), so I feel comfortable communicating with both of them as well as Farley (Paul McFarland). Knowing them and having worked with them makes it a good fit."

Misha Donskov Joined The Edmonton Oilers As A Coaching Consultant

Babcock, who reached out to Donskov, said that the club was excited to have him on board.

"We are excited to have Misha join our coaching staff," Babcock said . "We believe his wealth of experience, people skills and professionalism will make our group better. We look forward to the positive impact he will have on our staff, players and the Oilers organization."

Meanwhile, Hockey Canada knows that it's a tremendous opportunity for him.

"We consider this a tremendous experience for Misha, especially as we prepare to host the World Juniors with him as our head coach in December," said Scott Salmond, Senior Vice President of High Performance and Hockey Operations with Hockey Canada. "Misha is a proven winner and a tremendous leader, and we are excited that he will continue to develop his skills through this new position with the Edmonton Oilers, which we know will positively impact both of our organizations on and off the ice."

Donskov Will Still Work With Hockey Canada

Although Donskov has joined the Oilers, he will remain in his role as Hockey Canada's vice president of hockey operations and coach of its national men's team.

The London, Ontario native previously spent two seasons behind the bench with the Dallas Stars before joining the Vegas Golden Knights, where he worked in coaching and hockey operations for seven years and helped the club capture the 2023 Stanley Cup.

articles.title: Colorado stuns Georgia Tech on late touchdown pass
articles.summary: A late touchdown drive gave Colorado a road victory over Georgia Tech in the Buffaloes' season opener.
articles.body:
For 58 minutes, Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis didn't look ready for Prime -- Coach Deion Sanders -- or prime time.

Good thing for the Carrolton, GA, five-star player the game against Georgia Tech on Thursday was 60 minutes.

Lewis, who had thrown for 64 yards until the final drive, passed for 60 on the Buffaloes' final march. It concluded with 37 seconds left when he found Charlie Williams for a wheel route that went 20 yards and into the end zone.

The PAT gave the Buffaloes a 14-13 lead and they held on by blocking a last-gasp 45-yard field goal by the Yellow Jackets' Aidan Burr.

Georgia Tech started its last drive on the 25 and the first play saw Alberto Mendoza -- yes, he is Heisman winner Fernando's brother -- for 42 yards.

Georgia Tech put the ball in position for a field goal attempt but the Buffaloes blocked it and had a victory.

articles.title: Four Cardinals Prospects Acquired at MLB Trade Deadline Thriving in Minor Leagues
articles.summary: It's been a month since the Cardinals dealt veterans Dustin May, JoJo Romero and Lars Nootbaar, and the Cardinals appeared to have landed some promising pros...
articles.body:
The Cardinals announced to the baseball world that theywere in rebuilding mode last winter when they traded Nolan Arenado, Sonny Gray,Willson Contreras and Brendan Donovan for a host of Minor League prospects.

Then, they backed up those actions by doing more of thesame at the MLB Trade Deadline by shipping veteran pitchers Dustin May and JoJoRomero to the Brewers and outfielder Lars Nootbaar to the Dbacks for fourprospects.

With it being a month since the Aug. 3 Trade Deadline dealsbetween the Cards and Brewers and Cards and Dbacks, let's take a look at howthe former St. Louis players have fared and how the two transactions haveworked out so far.

Brewers receive right-handed starter Dustin Mayand left-handed reliever JoJo Romero. May, who was 5-7 with a 4.38ERA in 21 starts with the Cardinals, has mostly struggled with the Brewers andwas recently hit with some tough luck. May is 1-2 with a 6.41 ERA over fivestarts with Milwaukee. He was hit hard by the Mariners (seven hits, sevenearned runs in two innings pitched) and Rangers (six hits, four earned runs in4 1/3 innings pitched) and literally hit hard in a one-pitch start against theMets. New York's AJ Ewing drilled a 106-mph liner on the game's first pitch, andit hit off May's right shoulder blade. He left that game after just one pitchand luckily escaped with just a bruise.

Romero, 29, missed his final three weeks with the Cardinalsafter needing an emergency appendectomy over the break for the MLB All-StarGame. After going on a rehab assignment with the High-A Wisconsin TimberRattlers, Romero was activated on Sept. 1. In two games, Romero has yet to giveup a run while registering one hold out of the Milwaukee bullpen.

Cardinals receive Class-A outfielder AlexanderFrias and Double-A outfielder Josiah Ragsdale. MinorLeague talent evaluators were somewhat shocked that the Cardinals could pryaway the 6-foot-2 Frias, who was immediately installed as the No. 4 prospect inthe Cardinals' Minor League system. The 18-year-old Frias, who was signed to a$350,000 international free-agent deal out of the Dominican Republic in Januaryof 2025, has played 22 games with Class-A Palm Beach thus far. He's smashedfour doubles, a triple and two home runs to build a .749 OPS. He's also flashedby dynamic speed by swiping six bases.

As for Ragsdale, 22, he has continued his stellar season withDouble-A Springfield. In 23 games with the Cards, he has four doubles, atriple, five homers and 13 RBI. He's also stolen five bases in five tries. Infour Minor League stops in 2026, Ragsdale – the No. 11-ranked prospect in theCards' system – has racked up 25 doubles, 24 homers and 36 stolen bases while hitting.308 with a 1.001 OPS.

Diamondbacks receive outfielder Lars Nootbaar. The 28-year-oldoutfielder, who was a fan favorite in St. Louis for his infectious smile andfun-loving nature, got off to a slow start with Arizona. His first homer didn'tcome until his 12th game with the Dbacks and he smashed homers onback-to-back days on Aug. 28 and 29 in San Francisco. The final one was a grandslam. In 22 games with a DBacks team pushing for a playoff spot, Nootbaar ishitting .224 with four doubles, three homers and 11 RBI.

Cardinals receive right-handed starter DanielEagen and left-handed reliever Sandro Santana. Eagen,23, registered a 10-strikeout performance and an 11-strikeout performance sixdays apart in August for Double-A Springfield. The No. 22-ranked prospect is just2-3 with a 4.03 ERA in the hitter-friendly Texas League, but he has piled up animpressive 37 strikeouts in 29 innings of work. Foes are hitting just .206against Eagen.

Santana, 21, has been so impressive that he's alreadyearned a promotion from Double-A Springfield to Triple-A Memphis. In 9.2innings of work, Santana – who features a frisbee-like sweeper – has allowedjust two hits and one earned run. Incredibly, he has struck out 19 whilewalking none since becoming a member of the Cardinals organization.

articles.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves Roasted by Girlfriend Before Training Camp
articles.summary: Lakers star Austin Reaves' girlfriend, Jenna Barber, isn't impressed with his preparation for the new season. The post Lakers’ Austin Reaves Roasted by Girlf...
articles.body:
After inking a four-year max deal with the Los Angeles Lakers this summer, Austin Reaves is gunning to make his first All-Star team. But his girlfriend, Jenna Barber, isn't impressed with his preparation for the new season.

Earlier this week, Jenna poked fun at Reaves' form during a core crunch routine. In the video, Reaves could be seen falling to the ground and struggling to get through a set of crunches. Barber let it be known that the women in the session were more flexible.

"💪 Phys ED 😅 / Girls had way better form," she wrote [H/T New York Post].

For the first time in his career, Reaves will enter training camp as the clear-cut No. 2 option on the Lakers. Last year, he found himself in a similar role but only after LeBron James took a backseat and enabled the younger Reaves and Luka Doncic to take over.

Reaves responded by averaging a career-high 23.3 points, 5.5 assists and 4.7 rebounds on 49% shooting. He missed the early portion of the playoff series against the Houston Rockets with injury, but ultimately helped the Lakers advance to the second round.

AR-15 is ready to take his game to a new level after earning a massive payday.

"It's going to be fun," Reaves told The Athletic's Dan Woike of his expectations for the new season after signing a four-year, $185M deal.

"…Winning a championship is the main goal. And I feel like, you know, with me and Luka, that's a great starting piece to compete. When we put a roster together that can go compete, I feel like winning a championship will basically solidify everything that I want and everything that the Lakers want.

"It kind of meets the common goal of why they gave me the money they did."

With less than a month to go for training camp, the Lakers front office have some decisions to make. As of this writing, the Lakers have 16 players on guaranteed contracts, but are eligible to have only 15 on the roster at the start of the regular season.

Some reports suggest the Lakers could get through training camp and preseason before taking a final call on which player to cut/waive or trade. Other insiders believe the Lakers are not done making moves, linking them to wings such as P.J. Washington, Derrick Jones Jr. and Cam Whitmore, and even bigs such as Daniel Gafford.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton takes brutal ‘wittle feelings’ dig at Bucks fan after major U-turn on Pacers star
articles.summary: Tyrese Haliburton recently threw out the first pitch at a Chicago Cubs home game against his hometown Milwaukee Brewers. This led to a wild social media tiff...
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton recently threw out the first pitch at a Chicago Cubs home game against his hometown Milwaukee Brewers. This led to a wild social media tiff with a big Milwaukee sports fan.

Tyrese Haliburton was born and raised in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, only an hour and a half away from Milwaukee. Naturally, he grew up a fan of various franchises from the city like the Brewers and the Bucks.

Childhood fandom means little in the big leagues, though. When Haliburton faced the Bucks in the playoffs with the Indiana Pacers, he was pivotal in knocking them out in consecutive seasons.

This has earned him some animosity from his hometown fans. And after he threw out the ceremonial first pitch at a Chicago Cubs game on Thursday, the festering ill feelings boiled over on social media.

Tyrese Haliburton shows fan his own posts praising the Pacers star after being insulted

Nathan Marzion, a podcaster and popular Milwaukee sports fan, responded to a post on X about Hali throwing out the first pitch at Wrigley Field, saying, "If the Cubs lose, this is why."

Haliburton wasn't in the mood to be disrespected, and after Chicago secured a 2-1 win, wrote back saying, "We won, so what does that mean Nathaniel?"

Marzion replied, writing, "It means you're still the guy who went from a likeable hometown kid to someone who goes out of his way to be an a****** towards Milwaukee."

Hali's response was brutal, sharing pictures of Marzion's posts from back in the day that show he was a big believer in the superstar point guard.

The Pacers star wrote, "Is this how you talk about a*******? Or did I hurt your wittle feelings back to back years in April?"

The situation seems a bit sad, with hometown fans seemingly upset with Haliburton over things he cannot control. For his part, Hali doesn't seem particularly remorseful, either. Sports can be cruel.

articles.title: Southern 500 Preview: NASCAR’s Chase Begins at Darlington
articles.summary: The NASCAR Cup Series is officially entering championship mode. After 26 races of regular season competition, the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Chase begins Sunday...
articles.body:
The NASCAR Cup Series is officially entering championship mode.

After 26 races of regular season competition, the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Chase begins Sunday at one of the toughest tracks on the schedule: Darlington Raceway. The Cook Out Southern 500 will serve as the opening race of the 10 race championship battle, putting 16 playoff drivers under the microscope from the moment the green flag flies.

The race is scheduled for Sunday, September 6, at 5 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on USA Network, HBO Max, MRN Radio and SiriusXM NASCAR Radio. The 500 mile event will be the 27th points-paying race of the season.

Darlington Is the Perfect Playoff Opener

There may not be a better place to begin the Chase than Darlington.

Known as the "Lady in Black" and the "Track Too Tough to Tame," Darlington is a 1.366-mile egg-shaped oval that forces drivers to balance speed with survival. Turns 1 and 2 feature 25 degrees of banking, while Turns 3 and 4 have 23 degrees.

The unique shape of the track means drivers cannot simply find one perfect setup. Teams must find a compromise that works in both ends of the track, while tire wear and traffic can dramatically change the handling of the car throughout a long green-flag run.

At Darlington, the fastest line often brings drivers dangerously close to the outside wall. A small mistake can turn a potential top five finish into a destroyed race car.

That makes the Southern 500 less about simply having the fastest car and more about managing the race for 367 laps.

Two drivers enter Darlington with plenty of attention surrounding them: Tyler Reddick and Denny Hamlin .

Reddick already knows what it takes to win at Darlington. He won the track's spring race, the Goodyear 400, earlier this season, giving the 23XI Racing driver tremendous confidence heading into the playoff opener. He also enters the weekend as one of the early favorites to win the Southern 500.

Hamlin, meanwhile, enters the Chase as the No. 1 seed and the 2026 regular-season champion. His consistency throughout the season has made him one of the biggest championship favorites, and Darlington is a track where experience can be extremely valuable.

A strong performance Sunday could immediately put Hamlin in an excellent position for the rest of the opening playoff round.

One of the biggest storylines heading into the race is Chase Briscoe.

Briscoe has won the Southern 500 in each of the last two seasons, taking the checkered flag at Darlington in both 2024 and 2025. Now, he has a chance to do something extremely rare: win the race three consecutive times.

The last driver to win the Southern 500 three straight years was Jeff Gordon, who accomplished the feat four consecutive times from 1995 through 1998.

Briscoe will have to overcome a loaded playoff field to make history, but his recent success at the track makes him one of the drivers nobody can afford to overlook.

While the championship favorites will receive most of the attention, Darlington has plenty of potential dark horses.

Erik Jones is an obvious name to watch. The LEGACY MOTOR CLUB driver is a two-time Darlington winner and has recorded 10 top 10 finishes in 17 career starts at the track. He also finished 10th in the spring race this season.

Carson Hocevar is another driver capable of making noise. The young Spire Motorsports driver has shown plenty of speed on larger ovals this season and enters the playoffs looking to make his presence known.

Ross Chastain could also be a factor. His recent performances have provided momentum heading into the Chase, and Darlington presents an opportunity for the Trackhouse Racing driver to make an early statement.

The Southern 500 will feature a 38 car field, including all 16 Chase drivers.

Two non-chartered entries are also entered: Corey Heim will drive the No. 67 Toyota for 23XI Racing, while Chad Finchum will pilot the No. 66 Ford for Garage 66.

With the championship battle beginning, every driver will have a different objective. Some will be looking for a win, some will be focused on stage points, and others may simply want to survive Darlington without suffering major damage.

Expect the Southern 500 to be a battle of patience.

The race is long, the tires will wear, and the track will change throughout the afternoon and evening. Drivers who attack too aggressively early could pay for it later, while those who protect their equipment may find themselves in position to win when the race reaches its final stages.

The biggest question may be whether Reddick can repeat his spring success or whether Hamlin, Briscoe or another playoff contender can steal the spotlight.

One thing is certain: the road to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship begins at one of the most unforgiving tracks in NASCAR.

And at Darlington, surviving the "Lady in Black" may be just as important as winning.

articles.title: 3 Most Important Grizzlies Players for a Surprise 2026-27 Playoff Run
articles.summary: Cameron Boozer, Ty Jerome and Jerami Grant could determine whether the Memphis Grizzlies exceed expectations and make a surprise playoff run.
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies aren't expected to make the 2026-27 NBA playoffs, but pundits can't quite rule it out either. If they do make a playoff run, there are three players who will be most pivotal to their success.

Granted, that's an oversimplification. It will take a group effort for Memphis to make the playoffs. Still, like any team, there is a hierarchy.

This is not a ranking of long-term importance. This is about who can lead a playoff charge in 2026-27. The Grizzlies will need all hands on deck.

But these three players will matter more than anyone else.

Spoiler alert: Zach Edey is not on this list.

He'd be the first honorable mention. A full season of health from Edey could go a long way for the Grizzlies, but if he can't stay on the floor, Isaiah Stewart is one of the best backups in the NBA.

By contrast, the Grizzlies' wing rotation is mostly young. The veteran Grant could be a stabilizing force. If he begins to suffer age-related decline, the Grizzlies can kiss their playoff chances goodbye.

Memphis reportedly has no plans to trade Grant this season , which gives him a chance to play an important role for this young group.

In the meantime, there's another player whose health they should cross their fingers for.

If you're a regular Roundtable reader, you've heard this before: Ty Jerome was excellent in the mere 15 games he suited up for in 2025-26.

If the Grizzlies are going to make a postseason run this year, he'll need to play at least 40 more games than that.

We've also named Jerome as a trade candidate in these pages . That remains the most likely option if he's healthy heading into the deadline. Again, the Grizzlies are not projected as a playoff team.

Still, it's reasonable to say that if they are on track for the postseason, Jerome will inevitably be a significant reason why.

Is this a lot of weight to put on a rookie's shoulders? You bet.

The Grizzlies will rely on Boozer as a primary creator in 2026-27. That's not due to their playoff aspirations — it's a long-term strategy. The Grizzlies will want to get Boozer as many on-ball reps as they can, as quickly as possible.

The No. 3 overall pick will inevitably struggle. Almost every NBA rookie does. The question is whether he can perform better than the average rookie.

Boozer looks NBA-ready, and if that comes to fruition, this team could have enough talent around him to maximize his abilities and make a playoff run.

ABERDEEN, S.D. (KELO) — It was another solid night at Dacotah Bank Stadium in Aberdeen where the Northern State Wolves moved to 2-0 for the first time in 23 years with a 31-16 win over conference rivals, Winona State.

The Wolves offense continued to run on Kraft, Hank that is as the running back scored two touchdowns in the first quarter. The first, a 92-yard house call and the second a 3-yard receiving one out of the backfield.

The Warriors would make it 21-16 on a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter, but Kraft would break a 47-yard touchdown the next time to put this game to bed, before another field goal made it a 15 point game, where it would hold the rest of the way.

Kraft once again was over the 200-yard rushing mark as he carried the ball 22 times for 241 yards and 2 touchdowns, not to mention his six receptions for 33 yards and another touchdown, NSU has a real difference maker in the backfield.

NSU had two quarterbacks throw passing touchdowns, Joey Dube-Garrett went 10-of-18 for 101 yards and a score while Ty Englehart went 6-for-11 for 45 yards and a score.

Defensively, Jake Adams led with 17 total tackles followed by Cooper Logan (8) and Elijah Jopp and Javonnee Szymanski (6 each). Landon Kelley recorded the only turnover of the game for the Wolves via an interception.

Up next, the Wolves travel to Southwest Minnesota State next Saturday for an NSIC matchup with the Mustangs, kickoff is set for 5PM.

articles.title: How Colorado beat Georgia Tech with blocked FG despite not having a special teams coordinator
articles.summary: Here's how Colorado came away with the late-second win.
articles.body:
Colorado picked up a big Week 1 victory to kick off Deion Sanders' fourth season as head coach, scraping by Georgia Tech 14-13.

The Buffaloes struggled to score all night, but then came away with the game-winning touchdown late in the game. When the Yellow Jackets were quickly able to get into field-goal range, Colorado's special teams unit came up big with the game-saving play.

What makes the win more impressive is that it was Colorado's first without a special teams coordinator. Sanders decided not to fill the position as part of a slew of coaching staff changes in the offseason, and that gamble has so far paid off.

Here's how Colorado came away with the late-game win. MORE: Inside Colorado's QB depth chart

Colorado beats Georgia Tech with blocked kick

Colorado survived Week 1 against Georgia Tech thanks to a game-saving play from its special teams unit. The Buffaloes scored a late touchdown to take a one-point lead with under a minute left, but surrendered a big play to the Yellow Jackets that put Georgia Tech in field goal position.

As Georgia Tech kicker Aidan Birr attempted the game-winning kick, the Buffaloes successfully blocked the attempt to escape with the win.

Why doesn't Colorado have a special team coordinator

Prior to the season, Deion Sanders announced that the team would not have a dedicated special teams coordinator in 2026. Instead, Sanders is having each of his assistants help chip in with special teams coordinator duties.

Uncle Neely, who hosts Thee Pregame Show, confirmed that Sanders decided on the collabortive approach.

"What he's taken in this [year's] approach is more ownership as far as the coaches that you depend on to feed into special teams," Neely said in March . "The guys who coach the [defensive backs], the guys who coach the tight ends, the guys who coach the linebackers, etcetera, they're all now having a say in special teams."

Neely did add that tight ends coach Josh Niblett was likely to have more of a say in special teams duties than most other assistants. MORE: What to know about Shilo Sanders' bankruptcy trial

Who was Colorado's special teams coordinator last year?

Colorado's special teams coordinator in 2025 was Michael Pollock, who had worked under Sanders for the previous five years. Pollock began with Sanders at Jackson State and moved to Boulder with him in 2023.

Pollock said he understood that the change was coming after a disappointing 3-9 season and the split was amicable between both sides.

articles.title: Seahawks Trade Addition Drops ‘Legendary’ Message After Joining Seattle
articles.summary: Rookie cornerback Avery Smith already sounds comfortable with the standard attached to playing defense in Seattle.Smith met with reporters Thursday after joi...
articles.body:
Rookie cornerback Avery Smith already sounds comfortable with the standard attached to playing defense in Seattle.

Smith met with reporters Thursday after joining the Seattle Seahawks from the Los Angeles Chargers, and the former Toledo standout didn't undersell the history he's stepping into.

"Legendary defenses are built in Seattle. LOB and now you got the MOB," Smith said, referring to the Legion of Boom and the current Seahawks' MOB mantra.

The comment came after Smith described the Aug. 30 trade as a surprise. Seattle sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to Los Angeles for the undrafted rookie.

"Surprising. Can't be mad at that; I am glad and excited to be a Seahawk," Smith said. He added that he is learning the playbook and said the process is "going well."

The bigger challenge now is carving out a role in a secondary attached to some of the highest expectations in football.

Smith Embraces Seahawks' Defensive Standard

Smith's "legendary" description makes sense after the season Seattle just completed.

The Seahawks won Super Bowl LX 29-13 over the Patriots in February, with their defense holding New England scoreless through three quarters and producing six sacks and three takeaways. Seattle also allowed the fewest points in the NFL during the regular season, while its defense finished No. 1 in DVOA and eighth among defenses measured since 1978.

That group became known as "The Dark Side," while MOB — short for "Mission Over" an expletive — developed into a broader team mantra under Mike Macdonald. Smith loosely tied it to the Legion of Boom during his first week in Seattle, showing he already understands the lineage surrounding the franchise's defense.

He's joining a cornerback group headlined by Devon Witherspoon , while veteran Trevon Diggs is on the practice squad after Seattle's final roster cuts.

So, Smith has an opportunity to learn behind established players and potentially earn a role in sub-packages and on special teams. Seattle's call to acquire him suggests the Seahawks saw more than a developmental flier.

Seahawks Bet Draft Pick on Smith's Versatility

The Chargers signed Smith as an undrafted free agent in May after four seasons at Toledo. He appeared in 51 college games , totaling 127 tackles, three interceptions and 29 passes defensed.

Smith then produced 15 tackles and one pass defensed across three preseason games for Los Angeles. The Chargers described him as having a strong training camp, but a veteran-heavy cornerback depth chart made him expendable when general manager Joe Hortiz turned Smith into a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Smith also brings an interesting background to the position. He played quarterback growing up, with Cam Newton serving as one of his role models, and originally went to Toledo as a quarterback before moving to cornerback. His Seahawks bio notes that Smith threw for 3,208 yards and rushed for 913 yards as a high school senior.

It's that type of offensive experience can help a defensive back understand route concepts and a quarterback's intentions, even as Smith adjusts to a much more complex NFL scheme.

The rookie said he can play across the back end, and his college production points to a player willing to tackle as well as cover.

There's no guarantee Smith will have a defensive role right off the bat when Seattle opens the season against the Patriots on Sept. 9. He arrived only days before Week 1 and is still digesting Macdonald's system.

Nonetheless, Smith has already made clear what he believes he joined.
