articles.title: Ex-Kings announcer loses appeal over firing for ‘All Lives Matter' tweet
articles.summary: A federal appeals court ruled Thursday against former Sacramento announcer Grant Napear, who was fired in 2020 after responding to a former Kings player's qu...
articles.body:
A broadcasting company was entitled to fire a radio announcer who was also the play-by-play announcer for the Sacramento Kings of the NBA, after he tweeted "All Lives Matter" to a former Kings basketball player who asked him a question on the social media platform after the death of George Floyd, a federal appeals court ruled Thursday.

Grant Napear had been the Kings' announcer for 31 years and was also the host of a daily show on KTHK in Sacramento in May 2020, when Floyd was killed by a Minneapolis policeman who knelt on his neck and was later convicted of murder.

Napear claimed he was off work and following coverage of the protests when Demarcus Cousins , a former Kings player then with the Los Angeles Lakers who is Black, asked him on the platform (now known as X), "What's your take on BLM?," referring to the popular movement known as Black Lives Matter that began as a protest against racism and police brutality.

Napear responded with a tweet saying he was glad to hear from Cousins and that "ALL LIVES MATTER … EVERY SINGLE ONE!!!", wording often used by opponents of Black Lives Matter.

Bonneville International Corp., which employed Napear on his radio program and also as the Kings announcer, suspended him the next day and fired him a day later. He turned to podcasting for the next five years, but got a new broadcasting job last August as a daily host on Fox Sports Radio in Sacramento.

His lawsuit accused Bonneville of punishing him for private speech that was unrelated to his job. But the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco said Thursday that the broadcast company had acted legally to protect its own reputation.

"Napear was a public figure in his role as a radio-show host," and his contract "required him to maintain 'a high standard of care and level of responsibility' on social media, since it also affects the company's 'public image and reputation,'" the three-judge panel said , quoting the contract.

California law does not appear to "prevent employers from limiting employees' political expression undertaken within the scope of their employment such that it impacts the public reputation" of the employer, the court said, and Napear's use of his Twitter account "involved his celebrity persona such that his statement fell within the scope of his professional capacity."

The panel, drawn at random, consisted of Judges Bridget Bade, Danielle Forrest and Lawrence VanDyke, all appointed by President Donald Trump. They upheld a ruling by U.S. District Judge Dale Drozd of Sacramento, an appointee of President Barack Obama, dismissing Napear's suit without a trial.

Napear is not the first public figure to have been fired for his activities in social media, or the first sports broadcaster. One was Mike Bacsik, a former major league pitcher who was fired by a Dallas radio station in 2010 after a disparaging social-media posting about "Mexicans in San Antonio."

Napear's attorney, Matthew Ruggles, said he would ask the full appeals court for a new hearing before a larger panel, and, if that fails, seek review in the Supreme Court. He disputed the appeals court's conclusion that Napear's tweet was an "official" act related to his job.

"Grant Napear actually owned that Twitter account, had published approximately 38,500 tweets before he tweeted 'All Lives Matter…Every Single One,' and that tweet was not made on-air, during work, or as part of any radio show," Ruggles said. "It was Grant's personal expression, and that issue should be decided by a jury, not the court."

articles.title: Andrew Wiggins is ecstatic about his reunion with fellow champion Klay Thompson
articles.summary: Andrew Wiggins is pleased to reunite with a teammate he won a championship with back in 2022.
articles.body:
Now that Klay Thompson has joined the Miami Heat , he seems intent on adding another championship to his four rings from his Golden State Warriors days. The most recent win was in 2022, when he was also teammates with a certain Andrew Wiggins.

With this latest move to the Heat , Thompson has reunited with Wiggins. It is a touching reunion between the two former Warriors , and they now have a common goal once again. This time, it will be to help the Heat succeed in the Eastern Conference.

Andrew Wiggins loves that he gets to play with Klay Thompson again

For a long time, Thompson was one of the Warriors' focal points. He and Stephen Curry formed the Splash Brothers, the league's most dangerous shooting duo. In 2024, Thompson ended his 13-year run with the Warriors to join the Dallas Mavericks in free agency.

He was intent on playing alongside Luka Doncic, but unfortunately, the front office had different plans because they traded the Slovenian superstar just a few months later. With that move, it ended the championship window for the Mavericks , so Thompson wanted out.

After securing a buyout with the Mavericks, Thompson was free to sign with any team in the league. He felt that Miami was the best destination, and it seems that he is being accepted by the fans, the franchise, and a former teammate of his. Wiggins himself loves that he has another familiar face playing alongside him.

"He's one of the most competitive people I played with. To have him on the squad is going to be amazing. He's one of one. He brings that championship mentality to the team, and this is a year that we can do something special, and he's someone that can be a big part of it," Wiggins said about Thompson on the Heat's social media page .

Thompson and Wiggins will be important pieces for head coach Erik Spoelstra's system. If they can play within their roles, the Heat could compete with the best teams in the Eastern Conference for a shot at the NBA Finals.

articles.title: Collins, Murrell lead Kennesaw State's offensive eruption in 47-0 win over West Georgia
articles.summary: Rickie Collins accounted for three touchdowns and Latrelle Murrell ran for two touchdowns and Kennesaw State beat West Georgia 47-0 in the Owls' season opene...
articles.body:
KENNESAW, Ga. (AP) — Rickie Collins accounted for three touchdowns and Latrelle Murrell ran for two touchdowns and Kennesaw State beat West Georgia 47-0 in the Owls' season opener on Thursday night.

It was Kennesaw State's first shutout since a 14-0 win at home against North Carolina on Oct. 16, 2021.

Kennesaw State took advantage of Triston Morgan's 47-yard opening kickoff return which started at the goal line. On the fifth play of the drive, Murrell ran to his left and 45 yards later made it 6-0 before a missed point-after attempt.

Morgan ran for a 60-yard touchdown on a one-play drive to extend the margin to 12-0 before a failed two-point conversion.

On the ensuing kickoff, Sean Ferguson fumbled at the Wolves' 14 and Josh Anglin recovered it for Kennesaw State. Collins ran it in from the 3 with 44 seconds left for a 19-0 lead after one quarter.

Murrell made it 26-0 after a 17-yard touchdown run ended a four-play, 62-yard scoring drive with 6:18 before halftime. Collins ran it in from 24 yards out and Boogie Woods III crashed in from a yard out for a 40-0 advantage at halftime.

Collins threw his second touchdown pass — a 9-yarder — to Dylan Gary to close the scoring with 9:19 left in the third.

Collin Hurst threw for 93 yards for the Wolves.

articles.body:
COLMAN, S.D. (KELO) - #5 Colman-Egan picked up a dominate 52-14 win over the Arlington Cardinals on Thursday, extending the Hawks undefeated start to 3-0.

The Hawks, who started out the game up 8-0, had a chance to extend their lead to two touchdowns, but trouble with a toss in the backfield led to an Arlington scoop-and-score by senior captain Greyson Nielson. It cut the Colman-Egan lead to two points, but just a few plays later, with sophomore running back Landen McManus breaking free for a long touchdown run that made it 14-6.

The Hawks took a narrow 20-14 lead into the halftime break, but would outscore the Cardinals 32-0 in the second half, powering Colman-Egan to a 38-point victory. The Hawks have won all three of their games by 20 or more points, and have outscored opponents by an average of 33.3 per game.

Both teams will have an eight-day break before getting back in action on Sep. 11. Arlington will welcome Oldham-Ramona-Rutland High School (0-2) to Gilbertson-Anderson Field. Colman-Egan, however, will go to battle with the number one St. Mary's (2-0) on the road.

articles.title: Lions sophomore shines, continues family legacy at Lackawanna Trail
articles.summary: FACTORYVILLE, PA(WBRE/WYOU)— Another season of Lackawanna Trail Field Hockey is underway, and the Lions are off to a fast start once again. That is thanks in...
articles.body:
FACTORYVILLE, PA(WBRE/WYOU)— Another season of Lackawanna Trail Field Hockey is underway, and the Lions are off to a fast start once again. That is thanks in part to sophomore Lyla Ryon. The second year star already has five goals in just her first two games.

Ryon produces with the ball and without it. She led the team in goals and assists her freshman year. The feat earning her an all-state honorable mention.

Her success is a long time in the making, Lyla started training in second grade. Continuously playing above her age level wearing the Red, White, and Blue.

"When I was in the summer going into eight grade, I got invited into the USA national camp, and that definitely boosted my confidence. I was on the u16 USA team as a u14 athlete," said Ryon.

Alongside her, Ryan's built chemistry with teammate Emma Thomas. A foundation on the field that is built on trust between the two.

"Over the years, we just learned to trust each other. Trust is a big thing in sports. It's just knowing when I hear her voice, I just know that what she is telling me to do is going to work out like I have no doubt when I have Lyla on the field," Thomas said.

Head Coach Holly Colvin witnessed that talent display firsthand in her first two years at trail. "I can remember her playing in her backyard. So, she has always had a stick in her hand. You could tell she loved the sport from day one. For a freshman, it was beyond where you typically are."

Having good genes doesn't hurt either, her sister Leena is second in school history in goals. Her brother Isaac is also breaking several conference rushing records on the football field.

Lyla said, "Growing up watching my two siblings definitely helped me a lot just watching me see what they could do and achieve things that they achieved definitely pushed me to be better or even as good as them."

The Lions have district and a state title appearance on their minds for the first time since 2023, which just so happened to be Leena Thomas's senior season.

Congratulations once again to our 28/22 sports athlete of the week, Lyla Ryon!

articles.title: Satellite, Merritt Island Christian football win blowout games
articles.summary: Satellite improved to 4-0 after a 35-2 win over Seabreeze behind another stout defensive performance and an efficient offense.
articles.body:
After two convincing road wins, Satellite returned home to face its stiffest test of the season in FHSAA Class 4A Seabreeze in a matchup of unbeatens.

The Scorpions mirrored the same recipe of success as they did in their first three games. Thanks to a tenacious defense and an efficient offense, they earned a 35-2 win.

"Just real proud of them," Satellite head coach Dan Burke said. "We prepared a short week and the kids prepared hard. It's kind of a rivalry and our guys came out and played well in every facet of the game."

Satellite's defense pitched another shutout, extending its shutout streak to 188:41. The Sandcrabs scored a safety on a high snap off a punt that was recovered in the end zone.

Seabreeze entered Scorpions territory on three of its 10 possessions. It punted the ball six times.

"They were flying around, making plays," Burke said. "Proud of them. They prepare hard too."

Scorpions linebacker Anthony Romero made the first statement with a punishing hit on Seabreeze quarterback Noah Bogdanowicz, jarring the ball loose with defensive lineman Max Lopez recovering the fumble.

In the third quarter, linebacker Luke Herte lowered his shoulder for a big hit on Sandcrabs wide receiver Danny Spada, popping the ball in the air and leading to an interception for defensive back Kade Whitworth.

"All these guys, you'll find plays like Kade Whitworth. Somebody different steps up. Levi Mumme breaking up passes," Burke said. "It's a great team effort. It's fun to watch. They play the way you're supposed to play. Proud of the effort and the teamwork."

The Satellite offense fed off the defense, scoring 3 touchdowns off 3 takeaways. Quarterback Brody Grennan finished the night with 155 passing yards and 2 touchdowns. Three rushers scored touchdowns.

"We came out and punched them in the mouth. It was a great team effort. Controlled the ball. We didn't have many mistakes on offense. Proud of the team," Grennan said. "We got to come back Monday and get ready for Pine Ridge, but that's a statement win for our team. I feel like a lot of people were questioning how good we were. That definitely proves we're a good team."

Grennan connected with wide receiver Noah Corriveau on both touchdown passes. The signal caller evaded a sack in the pocket and launched a deep ball to Corriveau, who shed a tackle for an 80-yard score. Corriveau caught a 33-yard touchdown pass to cap the first drive of the second half.

"Me and Noah (Corriveau) have been playing together since we were like 10. Me and him are like best friends. We're always together and I feel like that helps a lot," Grennan said. "We communicate so well on the field. Everything is just simple. It's easy. Just give him the ball and he could score."

After Romero's strip sack, running back Raiden Kerr raced to the end zone on a 40-yard run to open the scoring. Herte scored a 1-yard touchdown on the ensuing drive following his big hit that lead to the interception. A fumbled kickoff by Seabreeze set up tailback Tristan Sejeck for a 1-yard touchdown run.

"The running game is always amazing," Grennan said. "It takes a lot off me and it's really easy to just pound the ball and tire them out. That's what we did. We tired them out."

Satellite improved to 4-0 and will return to SSAA play versus Pine Ridge on Sept. 11. Grennan said the confidence is sky high.

"Space Coast, a great win. That was a great team. The other two games, we should have won those games," Grennan said. "After this one, we just shot ourselves up there higher and higher and the momentum is going to be as high as possible. The next two games are good teams. It's the start of our gauntlet and we got to keep going. We have momentum, so I think we can."

In a rematch of last year's SSAA 8-man state quarterfinal, Merritt Island Christian prevailed after falling behind 6-0 following the first quarter.

The Cougars improved to 4-0 after winning their home opener. They have a bye week before returning to the field on Sept. 18 versus Academy at the Lakes.

articles.title: What does Boston College think of Cincinnati Bearcats ahead of opener?
articles.summary: Boston College speaks about opening their season at Nippert Stadium against the Cincinnati Bearcats Sept. 5
articles.body:
Boston College head coach Bill O'Brien's college coaching résumé spans Georgia Tech , Maryland, Duke, Penn State, Alabama, Ohio State (briefly), and now the Eagles of Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts .

In the NFL, he's been with the Patriots and was head coach of the Houston Texans.

Saturday, Sept. 5 marks the first head-to-head matchup between O'Brien and UC head coach Scott Satterfield when the Eagles come to Cincinnati. Both coaches need positive results out of the gate for their respective fan bases.

"Just like us, they have a lot of new players," O'Brien said. "Their secondary is out of the portal. They have a veteran offensive line that's very, very good. They have some transfers at wide receiver. So, we don't really know (about UC). We have an idea, but it's the first game, and there are a lot of unknowns."

The series is tied 4-4, but UC has won the last two, including the Jan. 2, 2020 Birmingham Bowl at Legion Field, 38-6. In that game, sophomore quarterback Desmond Ridder ran for three touchdowns and threw for another to take game MVP honors.

Before that, you have to go back to UC's 1997 Humanitarian Bowl championship season when they knocked off the Eagles 24-6 in Chestnut Hill. UC was down 6-0, but scored all 24 points in the final quarter with interception returns by Artrell Hawkins and Shawn Ferguson and a Chad Plummer 50-yard run.

Boston College's last win came Oct. 12, 1996, at Nippert Stadium, 24-17. Current BC general manager Kenyatta Watson had a touchdown catch that afternoon.

Boston College coach Bill O'Brien on new Bearcats

"They're really strong everywhere," O'Brien said. "They went out and got some really good players. They've got one guy that was a safety last year (Antwan Peek Jr.) that's going to play outside backer. Offensive line, defensive line, they've got depth. They've got at least five receivers of different size that are good route runners. They have a punter and placekicker who are NFL prospects and they have JC French (quarterback) who was so productive at Georgia Southern. It's a big challenge."

Boston College was 2-10 last season, winning their first and last games of the season. Their victory over Syracuse last November was their only road win. In 2024, they were 7-6, with their only road win coming two years ago, Sept. 2, 2024 in Tallahassee against then-No. 10 Florida State .

Cincinnati Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield on key Boston College players

Mason McKenzie is of similar size to JC French IV and threw for 2,086 yards and 17 touchdowns in addition to running for 942 yards and 10 scores with Saginaw Valley State last season. Satterfield says UC looked at him in the transfer portal when trying to replace Brendan Sorsby.

"He's a very talented player, dual-threat, can really run," Satterfield said.

articles.title: SDSU-Nebraska matchup breaks records, inspires growth
articles.summary: BROOKINGS, S.D. (KELO) — The South Dakota State University Jackrabbits volleyball team held its biggest home game in program history Wednesday night against...
articles.body:
BROOKINGS, S.D. (KELO) — The South Dakota State University Jackrabbits volleyball team held its biggest home game in program history Wednesday night against number one Nebraska. This game not only broke records, but served as a reminder of how far the game has come in South Dakota.

A record-breaking crowd of 5,113 people turned to a roar at the First Bank and Trust Arena in Brookings anytime the Jacks scored against number one Nebraska on Wednesday night.

This turnout marked the largest for a volleyball game in the state's history.

"I mean to play in front of 5,000 people in our home gym with the community of Brookings was just insane. I think this was so special for the state of South Dakota, for the volleyball in South Dakota. That was an unreal experience," SDSU senior outside hitter Sylvie Zgonc said.

SDSU Head Coach Dan Georgalas says this game served as a reminder of just how far the program has come.

"We had 255 fans in the spring of 2021. Our first season was canceled and now here we are playing the number one team in the country… I'm just so grateful. This place is so much bigger than any one person and our players know that," Georgalas said.

Nebraska is no strangers to record breaking volleyball crowds, but even their Head Coach Dani Busboom Kelly was impressed with Jackrabbit Nation.

"The crowd was awesome and they were into it and it was hostile . I thought there would be more red, so I think that was actually cool to see it be, you know, South Dakota State fans and them having a lot of pride," Busboom Kelly said.

This match also marked a homecoming for Nebraska Setter and O'Gorman High School graduate Bergen Reilly who had a large contingent of fans in the stands, including her older sister, Raegen, who played volleyball at SDSU.

"I knew quite a few people here. Had a lot of family here. She {Raegen} got to be here too so that was cool. Got out of some law school homework," Reilly said.

Reilly also took time post game to reflect on the state of volleyball in South Dakota where she believes progress is being made but there is work to do.

"It's awesome just how volleyball is growing around the country, but in South Dakota I think we've been just a little bit behind, so it's cool to see us starting to catch up and yeah this is a big testament to that," Reilly said.

The O'Gorman graduate added that it was an awesome experience to play in front of the largest volleyball crowd ever in her home state.

The Cornhuskers did in fact sweep the Jackrabbits in this matchup, however there is a silver lining as SDSU put up the most points in a set on Nebraska so far this year with 20 points in set two.

articles.title: Last-second blocked field goal leads Colorado, coach Deion Sanders to dramatic 14-13 win over Georgia Tech in opener
articles.summary: Colorado's defense and special teams came through in Colorado's 14-13 win over Georgia Tech.
articles.body:
Deion Sanders' special teams stepped up when it was prime time.

Boo Carter blocked Aidan Birr's 45-yard attempt at a game-winning field goal as time expired, and Colorado held on for a 14-13 win at Georgia Tech in its opener on Thursday night.

The win at least temporarily turned down the pressure on Sanders after last season's 3-9 finish.

Colorado had just taken the lead on Charlie Williams' 20-yard touchdown reception from Julian Lewis with 37 seconds remaining.

Alberto Mendoza -- in his first start at quarterback for Tech since transferring from Indiana -- completed a 42-yard pass to Dalen Penson on the first play of the final possession to give the Yellow Jackets hope. Three plays netted six yards to set up the final field goal attempt.

Colorado held Tech to 288 total yards. Mendoza -- the younger brother of 2025 Heisman Trophy winner Alberto Mendoza -- completed 17 of 23 passes for 237 yards for the Yellow Jackets in his first game since transferring from Indiana.

Tech's only touchdown came on Rahkeem Smith's 100-yard kickoff return early in the second quarter that tied the game at 7.

articles.title: Rutgers 'celebrates' devastating loss to UMass with postgame fireworks show
articles.summary: Rutgers added insult to its own injury with a fireworks show following its season opening loss to UMass.
articles.body:
Rutgers football paid $1.55 million to lose to UMass , 37-21 , on Sept. 3, snapping the Minutemen 's 16-game losing streak. But that number presumably didn't include pyrotechnics.

The Scarlet Knights hosted the saddest fireworks show in the world after the loss at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, putting a droopy exclamation point on an 0-1 start to Greg Schiano's seventh season.

It's the kind of loss that immediately puts a coach on the hot seat, and Rutgers will now have to reconcile what this means for the nation's oldest program. While the team has hardly been even middle-of-the-road in the college landscape since Schiano's first stint in 2001-2011, losing a buy game to a team that hadn't won a game since 2024 is program-shakingly bad.

The loss to UMass is arguably as bad or worse as losing to some FCS programs. Since joining the FBS in 2012, the Minutemen have been brutally bad, amassing a 26-134 record with six seasons with 11 losses or more.

Rutgers entered this game as a 29.5-point favorite. But even with nothing to celebrate, the show must go on.

articles.title: Becker loses to Orono in coach Dwight Lundeen's final season opener
articles.summary: Becker had control all game, but Orono would just not quit. The Spartans used a big fourth quarter to escape with a 35-28 win over Becker.
articles.body:
BECKER, MN — Entering the fourth quarter with a slim lead on Sept. 3, Becker took a commanding nine-point advantage with 7:48 left on the clock. In an outing that had been far from perfect, the Bulldogs could taste victory up two scores in the waning minutes of the game.

Then Orono senior quarterback Finn Dyvik found senior receiver Owen Paulson along the sideline for a 68-yard pitch-and-catch to score the first of 23 fourth quarter points for the Spartans to suck the out of Dwight Lundeen Stadium and escape with a win.

While it may not have been the storybook beginning to Becker's head coach Dwight Lundeen farewell tour after 57 seasons, the two most recent 4A champions did not disappoint as Orono bested Becker 35-28 thanks to its big fourth quarter effort.

Becker got the scoring started in the first half with a 14-0 lead heading into the locker room behind two first-half interceptions and a 40-yard touchdown reception from senior RJ Houle.

The reigning champs stayed calm, though. Coming out in the second half and scoring two unanswered touchdowns in the third quarter, including a second interception by Becker's senior quarterback Tristan Kowalkowski.

"We made a couple of adjustments on our defensive front and how we were playing coverage," Orono coach Joe McPherson said. "We were doing okay in the first half. We just were giving up the big play and getting our eyes wrong, so we got our eyes right in the second half."

As the fourth quarter progressed, the Bulldogs continued to unravel with a fumble on the kick return which led to Orono's second touchdown in just over a minute of gametime to take its first lead of the night.

Kowalkowski would find Houle for 59 yards — the longest of three big connections between the two — to set up a game-tying score by senior receiver Tarver Schendzielos, but the Spartans marched right down the field to get the go-ahead score with 34 seconds remaining with a sweep to Hudson Hirt.

In the end, it was just too many mistakes by Becker to dethrone the defending champs.

"I was proud of them," Lundeen said. "They played hard, but we just did enough things to cause us not to win. We snapped the ball over our head, we fumbled the ball on the three-yard line and we missed some assignments defensively that gave them some big runs. Those are all things we can fix."

Becker is on the road at Hutchinson on Sept. 11 for week two.

articles.title: White Sox Minor League Update: September 3, 2026
articles.summary: Playoff pushes highlight a perfect night on the farm
articles.body:
Charlotte Knights 1, Gwinnett Stripers 0 Pitching ruled the night as Charlotte (72-63) and Gwinnett locked horns for eight innings. Jonathan Cannon took the ball and delivered 5 1/3 shutout frames, allowing three hits and no walks while recording four punchouts. The bullpen was nails, hurling 3 2/3 scoreless innings while allowing just one hit — a single off Tanner McDougal to open the ninth. Shane Smith got some work in the seventh. Since skipper Chad Pinder shifted him to relief last week, Smith has rattled off three straight hitless outings, though he's handed out three free passes.

The bats were mostly sleepwalking, mustering seven singles, but they found the clutch hit in the ninth. Mario Camilletti poked a one-out base hit and scooted to second on a wild pitch. Riley Unroe drew a walk, and Dru Baker delivered the RBI knock. Rikuu Nishida promptly rolled into a double play, but the run had scored, and that was all Charlotte needed. Kyle Teel sat this one out; Korey Lee handled the catching duties, and Edgar Quero slotted in as the DH.

Postseason watch: The Knights are a dark horse for a playoff spot, but if they go on a hot streak, anything is possible.

Runners-Up Jonathan Cannon: 5 1/3 IP, 3 H, 0 R, 0 BB, 4 K Tanner McDougal: 2 IP, 1 H, 1 BB, 2 K, W Shane Smith: 1 IP, 0 H, 0 R, 2 BB Mario Camilletti: 2-for-4, R, K

Runners-Up Junior Perez: 0-for-3, BB, SB, 2 K Jake Cave: 0-for-3, BB

Birmingham Barons 3, Biloxi Shuckers 2 Birmingham (56-73) and Biloxi traded early jabs, then settled into a 2-2 deadlock that dragged from the third through the eighth. The Barons got on the board first, scoring on a bases-loaded walk, only for the Shuckers to punch back with two tallies in the bottom half. Anthony DePino, doing what he does, leveled things in the third with a solo blast, his 19th Double-A homer. Then the bats went silent.

Finally, the Barons broke through in the ninth. Jordan Sprinkle coaxed a one-out walk, swiped second and then watched Dylan Campbell reach on a pop-up that should have been routine. Chaos followed with a double steal, putting runners at second and third. Caleb Bonemer whiffed, but the third strike skipped away, allowing Sprinkle to dash home with the go-ahead run. Jackson Kelley gave up a one-out single in the bottom half but retired the next two batters. Ballgame.

Postseason watch: With first-place Rocket City losing, the third-place Barons moved to within one game of a playoff spot because second-place Knoxville already qualified by winning the first half.

MVP Anthony DePino: 2-for-3, R, 2 RBI, BB, HR, K

Runners-Up Jordan Sprinkle: 1-for-3, R, BB, 3 SB, OA, 2 K Dylan Campbell: 1-for-2, R, SB Carson Jacobs: 2 IP, 1 H, 0 R, 2 BB, 4 K Phil Fox: 1 IP, 0 H, 0 R, BB, W Jackson Kelley: 1 IP, 1 H, 0 R, K, S

Runners-Up Riley Gowens: 3 IP, 3 H, 2 R, 2 BB, 2 K, E Colby Shelton: 0-for-4, 2 K Jorge Corona: 0-for-4, 3 K Jacob Burke: 0-for-4, 2 K

Winston-Salem Dash 11, Rome Emperors 5 After falling behind 1-0 in the first, the Dash (72-56) pulled even on Nick McLain's sacrifice fly in the second. Rome grabbed the lead right back, but Winston-Salem got its act together in the fourth. Kyle Lodise worked a free pass, swiped second and hustled to third when George Wolkow reached on an error. Jeral Perez bounced into a double play, but Lodise crossed the plate anyway. James Taussig then uncorked a solo shot to put the Dash on top, 3-2.

Wes Kath and Rylan Galvan kicked off the fifth with back-to-back singles before Ely Brown bunted them over. After Javier Mogollón lined out, Lodise reached on yet another Rome miscue, allowing both runners to score. Perez went deep in the sixth, and the Dash kept the party going with five more runs, capped by a two-run Mogollón bomb in the ninth. Starter Justin Sinibaldi did enough for the win, allowing two runs, one earned, on four hits and two walks with three punchouts over five innings.

Postseason watch: With tonight's win, the Dash moved into first place, overtaking the playoff-bound Bowling Green Hot Rods. Winston-Salem holds a 2 1/2-game lead over the third-place Greenville Drive.

MVP James Taussig: 2-for-3, R, 2 RBI, BB, HR

Runners-Up Jeral Perez: 2-for-4, 2 R, RBI, HR Rylan Galvan: 2-for-4, 2 R, PB Javier Mogollón: 1-for-5, R, 2 RBI Justin Sinibaldi: 5 IP, 4 H, 2 R (1 ER), 2 BB, 3 K

Runners-Up Jesus Mendez: 1 1/3 IP, 3 H, 3 R, BB, K Kyle Lodise: 0-for-3, 2 R, 2 BB, SB, 2 K

Kannapolis Cannon Ballers 13, Delmarva Shorebirds 0 Kannapolis (69-60) ran wild in this one, racking up 14 hits and going an impressive 9-for-18 with RISP. The Ballers got things moving in the second inning with a little minor-league chaos. With two outs, Clay Burdette walked, swiped second and advanced on a wild pitch before Jake Berkland drew a walk. Cue the double steal — Burdette scored, and Berkland took third when the throw sailed somewhere into the Carolina night. Then Landon Hodge poked a single, Berkland trotted home and it was 2-0 Ballers.

Kanny wasn't done clowning the Shorebirds. With two outs in the third, Steven Lancia slapped a single, Grayson Fitzwater ripped an RBI triple and Alexander Albertus doubled him home.

Just like that, it was 4-0, and the rout was on. In the sixth, the Shorebirds' second baseman booted one, two more unearned runs crossed and it was 6-0. That should have been plenty, but Kannapolis kept piling, tacking on seven more runs over the final two frames. The eighth was a parade, with 12 hitters coming to the plate and six runs scoring without a single ball leaving the yard.

The arms were just as sharp. Gabe Tanner spun six shutout innings, scattering four hits and two walks while striking out three. The bullpen was equally impressive, with Luis Fonseca and Marco Barrios combining for three more scoreless innings and allowing just one lonely single.

Postseason watch: No playoffs for the Cannon Ballers. All the spots are clinched. They had a great second half though!
